stem.en: Put a signal's journey in order, from a hormone in the blood to a body that has changed.

text.en: A hormone from a gland fits a receptor on a cell's outside, and the fit bends the receptor's inside face.
The bent receptor makes cyclic AMP, and a relay of phosphate-adding shape changes amplifies the message.
The relay's last enzyme switches on glycogen phosphorylase, or, through a transcription factor, changes which genes are copied.
A nerve carries the fast version as a wave of gates, and spits a neurotransmitter across a synapse to a muscle.
Cells that stick, signal and flip different switches make tissues, organs and a body that holds its lines.
Every signal fades, so every line can be corrected, and a cell that goes deaf to stop is a lump.
